rendered: The authors did not train a machine-learning model such as a random forest or a neural network. The paper never mentions those methods or a support vector machine. To classify the bacteria they used the statistical method of linear discriminant analysis (LDA)[1]. The sensor-array responses were subse-quently analyzed using LDA[2], and the score plots were built from the two principal discriminant factors[3] (see Fig. 2[4]).[5] The authors also used unsupervised hierarchical cluster analysis (HCA[6] to group the species. The only places the phrase "machine learning" appears are the titles of cited references, not the authors' own methods.[7]
